name: crypto-horizon-1m
description: Predicts a Binance spot price one minute ahead, in basis points of the last close, and posts a market around it. The box also offers ask_opus, ask_sonnet and ask_gpt5_mini, which put the same state to a second chat model; this seed does not use them, because each one costs real money on every window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close, which is a narrower and mostly unanswerable question - and saying so, with zero, is the right answer most of the time.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium to spot snapping back through it
- the US cash open, and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: a surge of taker selling on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or has not finished extending

What does not:
- your view on the coin. The market has that already.
- the day's on-chain figures, which describe yesterday.

You answer with two numbers.

**How many basis points it moves.** Not where the price is - where it goes, relative to the last close. Zero is a real answer and usually the right one; a quiet tape at a quiet hour does not move two basis points in a minute. But zero is a decision, not a default, and if the tape has just turned you are expected to say so in basis points.

**How wide a market you post.** Half the width of the two-sided quote that goes on the book every cycle, in basis points. Five means you are bid five under your number and offered five over it, and both sides rest there until the path reaches them. This is a choice, not a reading of how unsure you are: a width the path travels through has both its sides taken at prices the market has already left behind, and a width nobody reaches never trades and costs nothing at all. The tick is two basis points; the path reaches a median of four and a half from the last close, and a tenth of minutes reach thirteen.

steps.name: predict

delta_bps.description: How many basis points the price will MOVE over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close. Negative for down, 0 for no move. Do not state a price - state the change.

half_width_bps.description: The half width, in basis points, of the two-sided market that is POSTED on your behalf every cycle: bid at (prediction - this) and offered at (prediction + this), a resting order that pays the maker fee. This is not a confidence band; it is a choice about what you are willing to trade. The path will travel through a width that is too narrow and take BOTH sides, at prices the market has already left behind - every one of those fills is adversely selected. A width nobody reaches never trades and costs exactly nothing, which is what standing aside costs. The one-minute path reaches a median of four and a half basis points from the last close and a tenth of minutes reach thirteen, so two is run over on one side or both in four minutes out of five. The venue tick is two basis points and anything under it is widened to it.

confidence.description: 0-1. How sure, given how noisy a single minute is.

driver.description: The one thing you expect to move it, or why nothing will.

falsifier.description: What would show this call was wrong, before the minute is up.

action.description: What the paper book should do in the perpetual now. open_long buys the coin at the ask and open_short sells it at the bid, each filled down the book at five basis points a side; close takes an open position off at the touch; hold does nothing. Trade only when the move you expect clears a round trip of about twelve basis points.

size.description: Fraction of the book's equity to put in this coin if opening, 0 to 0.10. 0 when holding or closing.
